script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for April 22. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
The wheel seems obvious—round things roll.  But humans built cities, wrote languages, and raised pyramids for thousands of years before inventing the wheel.  Simple doesn't mean easy to discover.

The first wheels weren't for carts—they were potter's wheels, spinning clay into vessels. Transportation wheels came later. The same principle—rotation on an axis—found its first use in art, not travel. A wheel is useless without an axle that fits precisely—too tight and it won't turn, too loose and it wobbles.  This two-part system required solving multiple problems simultaneously.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Obvious in hindsight doesn't mean obvious in foresight.  The wheel teaches humility—ideas that seem simple required genius to discover.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Hindsight Humility - Appreciate Discovery.

Here's your activity: Think of something you consider 'obvious.' Now imagine you lived before it existed. Would you have invented it? The wheel, zero, the scientific method—all were breakthroughs that seem inevitable only after they happened. This helps you develop appreciation for the difficulty of innovation.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about the invention of the wheel can be applied to hindsight humility - appreciate discovery. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
